entry.title: Building PolyScan: Free CC0 PBR Textures & 3D Models for Real Projects
entry.summary:
I’m a 3D artist and game developer, and over the years I’ve spent a lot of time working with PBR textures and 3D assets for games, environments, and real-time projects. During that time, I realized how important three things are for artists: That idea is what led me to build PolyScan.
PolyScan is a small but growing library of free CC0 PBR textures and 3D models created using real-world photogrammetry workflows. Every asset is processed with the goal of being immediately usable in production, no special setup, no hidden restrictions. What I focus on with PolyScan: Clean, consistent PBR maps (Albedo, Normal, Roughness, height 32bit etc.) Real-world scale and believable surface detail Assets that work well in Unreal Engine, Unity, and Blender A simple CC0 license, no signup, no attribution required
Most of the assets start as real-world scans and are carefully cleaned and optimized for real-time use. I try to keep everything practical, not experimental,the kind of assets you can drop into a scene and start working right away. This project is still evolving, and I’m improving the workflow with every new scan. PolyScan is built by an artist, for artists, with a focus on quality over quantity. If you’re a 3D artist or developer, I’d love to know: Thanks for reading.

entry.title: Unpacking the Google File System Paper: A Simple Breakdown
entry.summary:
Core Philosophy: Keep It Simple, Scale Big
GFS prioritizes simplicity, high throughput, and fault tolerance over strict consistency. Key ideas: Relaxed consistency: Trades strict data guarantees for performance. Single master: Simplifies metadata management but risks bottlenecks (minimized by design). Workload focus: Optimized for large files and sequential access, not small files. GFS has three main components: Master: Stores metadata (file structure, chunk locations) in memory for speed. Chunkservers: Store 64 MB data chunks, replicated (usually 3x) on local disks. Clients: Applications that get metadata from the master and data directly from chunkservers. The single master simplifies the design while staying lightweight by handling only metadata operations. Following early access periods and today's broader rollout, executives, developers, and analysts have taken to X (formerly Twitter) and company blogs to share their first testing results.
